name: edit_file
description:
Edit a file in place, in one of two modes. You must read the file first.

## STR_REPLACE mode
Give `old_string` + `new_string`. `old_string` must match EXACTLY, whitespace included. If it occurs more than once, add context or set `replace_all: true`.
```json
{"path": "file.py", "old_string": "def hello():", "new_string": "def greet():"}
```

## INSERT mode
Give `insert_line` + `new_string`. `insert_line: 0` inserts at the beginning of the file; `insert_line: N` inserts AFTER line N (N may be the last line). `new_string` may span several lines.
```json
{"path": "file.py", "insert_line": 5, "new_string": "    # New comment"}
```

**When NOT to use:** replacing most of a file — use write_file. If `no_match` persists on a large `old_string`, use INSERT mode or write_file.

Errors: `read_before_write` (read it first), `no_match` (old_string absent), `multiple_matches` (old_string ambiguous), `out_of_range` (insert_line outside 0..line count), `invalid_args` (neither or both modes given).

path.description: Path to the file to edit

old_string.description: STR_REPLACE mode: exact string to find and replace

insert_line.description: INSERT mode: insert AFTER this line (0 = beginning of file)

replace_all.description: STR_REPLACE mode: replace all occurrences (default: false)

inserted_after.description: the line the text now follows (0 = start of file)
